title: SLO rampdown + graceful degrade manager and regional escort hotfix
author: Maya Fernandes
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce SLORampdownManager and regional escort to reduce cross-region egress and stabilize circuit flips; telemetry added for SLO transitions.
description:
Context: Recent incident (SUP-4012) surfaced a storm of cross-region failovers that caused rapid circuit flips and SLO violations for a subset of customers in EU-west. Root cause: long-tail KV cache pressure combined with aggressive failover heuristics and an eager egress path that redirected in-flight traffic to alternate regions immediately, amplifying load. This PR introduces a defense-in-depth hotfix to reduce blast radius and stabilize failovers while preserving availability.

What this PR delivers (single-string summary): 1) SLORampdownManager: a lightweight controller that enforces gradual, measurable SLO relaxation for affected routes. Instead of the current binary fallback, we ramp non-essential work (telemetry sampling, prefetch, low-priority rerank) down over a configurable window, giving serving nodes headroom. 2) RegionalEscort: a short-lived routing mode that, when a region is under pressure, moves newly arriving connections to a warm standby region only after an egress budget check; existing in-flight requests are drained locally where possible. 3) CircuitStabilizer: debounce logic for circuit state transitions (open->half-open->closed) to avoid oscillation when health probes jitter. 4) EgressLimiter: per-tenant cross-region egress soft-cap with a fast-path throttle that prevents sudden spillover bursts. 5) Telemetry and audit: emit SLO state transitions, ramp stages, and egress budget events to the new slo.rampdown and net.egress metrics; wire those events into the console alerting playbook.

Motivation and tradeoffs: The goal is to limit customer-visible latency regressions while preventing cascade failovers. The rampdown approach favors progressive degradation (reduce features) over abrupt circuit-based failover. This means some features may be disabled temporarily for affected tenants, which is preferable to large-scale failovers. The egress limiter is conservative and respects tenant SLAs; we added safe defaults but exposed flags to tune behavior per-customer.

Implementation notes: - SLORampdownManager lives in runtime/control/slo_rampdown.go and is a small stateful actor that subscribes to NodeHealth and RouteLoad events. It uses an exponential backoff schedule for ramp steps and emits telemetry at every step. - RegionalEscort routing changes live in gateway/router/escort.go and add a soft handshake to ensure the target region reports warm capacity before shifting new connections. - CircuitStabilizer modifies circuit state machine in runtime/circuit/state_machine.go with a 3-stage hysteresis and a jitter-tolerant probe scheduler. - EgressLimiter is implemented as a middleware (gateway/middlewares/egress_limiter.go) with per-tenant counters backed by the runtime quota store. - Added unit tests and an integration canary that simulates KV pressure and validates ramp behavior without full cluster failover.

Testing and CI: - Unit tests added: slo_rampdown_test.go, escort_test.go (local), circuit_state_test.go. - Integration canary: canary/egress-rampdown-sim.yml that runs in perf-lab and asserts SLO regressions are limited to <1% for synthetic traffic while preventing >20% cross-region spill. - CI: initial run failed due to a flaky probe scheduling test; fixed by adding deterministic clock in CircuitStabilizer and re-ran. Final CI: all checks pass (build, unit, lint, integration-canary).

Files changed (high-level): runtime/control/slo_rampdown.go, gateway/router/escort.go, runtime/circuit/state_machine.go, gateway/middlewares/egress_limiter.go, telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new metrics), tests/{slo_rampdown_test.go, escort_test.go, circuit_state_test.go}, canary/egress-rampdown-sim.yml

Commits summary: - 9f3a1d2: introduce SLORampdownManager and core ramping API - b7a4c2e: regional escort routing handshake and warm-check - 1c2b3f9: circuit stabilizer hysteresis + deterministic probe clock - 2d4e5f6: egress limiter middleware and quota hook - a7b8c9d: telemetry events and console playbook wiring - f0e1d2a: tests and integration canary - 0b0b0b0: fix flaky probe test (use fake clock)

Review notes and conversation (condensed into single string): - Jordan Lee: "Great approach; two quick asks — (1) can we make the default ramp window shorter for free-tier tenants to avoid throttling their UX? (2) please add an integration that asserts no regression to hosted-api latency under low load." — Maya: "(1) made ramp window configurable via runtime flags and default kept conservative; added docs for per-tenant overrides. (2) added a small low-load integration that runs in perf-lab; results included in canary output." - Priya Natarajan: "CircuitStabilizer looks good; ensure the hysteresis values are telemetry-friendly so SRE can tune quickly." — Maya: "Added slo.rampdown.* and circuit.stabilizer.* metrics and dashboard pointers in the PR description." - Carlos Rivera (approval): "LGTM after CI green. Make sure we add a follow-up to codify per-tenant SLA overrides in Dedicated plans." - Jordan Lee: "Approved — small nit about log levels changed to DEBUG for ramp steps to avoid noisy logs; updated." 

CI timeline: First run (02-19) — failed (probe test flake). Re-run after fake clock fix (02-21) — pass. Canary run (02-22) — pass with expected ramp characteristics. Merge performed 02-24 via squash.

Post-merge actions: - Deployed hotfix to staging (02-24) behind feature flag slo_rampdown.enabled=false. - Gradual roll to prod: enabled for 5% of traffic in EU-west first, monitor slo.rampdown.metrics; increased to 50% after 6 hours, full roll at 18 hours once telemetry confirmed stability. - Follow-up items created: ENG-3189 (per-tenant SLA config UI), ENG-3240 (expand egress budget telemetry), ENG-3251 (stress test harness extension).

Risks and mitigations: The main risk is over-aggressive ramping causing feature regressions for sensitive customers. Mitigation: per-tenant overrides, safe defaults, and rapid rollback via feature flag. Another risk is false-positive warm checks preventing legitimate failover; mitigated by a short retry window and conservative warm thresholds.

Summary: This PR provides a pragmatic, incremental hotfix to reduce cascade failovers and SLO violations by ramping non-essential work, stabilizing circuit transitions, and limiting cross-region egress. It is designed to be safe (feature-flagged), observable (rich metrics), and reversible. Merged to main and rolled out progressively.
